6119.name: A Small Path In The Deep, Dark Forest
6119.description:
The area is a narrow path leading through the deep, dark forest. Huge,
ancient trees are on all sides. The path continues north and south.
Branches intertwine overhead, filtering the light. The scent of pine and
earth fills the air.

north.description: The narrow path winds its way through the trees to the north.

south.description: The narrow path winds its way through the trees to the south.

6120.name: On The River Bank In The Deep, Dark Forest
6120.description:
The area is a narrow path leading through the deep, dark forest. To the
south a fast river is flowing westward through the forest. Ancient grey
trees loom on both banks. The path continues north and west. Ancient
trees rise on all sides. The forest floor is carpeted with fallen
leaves.

north.description: The narrow path winds its way through the trees to the north.

south.description: To the south lies On The Wooden Bridge.

west.description: The narrow path winds its way through the trees to the west.

6121.name: A Dead End Path On The River Bank In The Deep, Dark Forest
6121.description:
The area is a narrow path leading through the deep, dark forest. The
ancient trees stand so close that the path disappears between the dusty
roots. To the south a dark river flows from east to west. The only exit
appears to be east. The scent of pine and earth fills the air. Ancient
trees rise on all sides.

east.description: The narrow path winds its way through the trees to the east.

16300.name: On The Wooden Bridge

north.description: To the north lies On The River Bank In The Deep, Dark Forest.

south.description: To the south lies On The Riverbank In The Deep, Dark Forest.

16300.description:
The bridge is roofed with mossy shingles and walled with planks, a
covered crossing that keeps the worst of the spray off those who use it.
Through gaps between the boards the river can be seen rushing below,
loud enough to drown out speech. The floor timbers flex and creak with
every step. The bridge leads north to the far bank and south back into
the forest.

16301.name: On The Riverbank In The Deep, Dark Forest

north.description: To the north lies On The Wooden Bridge.

south.description: To the south lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

16301.description:
A fast river races past here, grey-green and cold, foaming white over
hidden rocks. A wooden bridge leads north across it, its planks dark
with spray. The bank is a tangle of roots and slick stones where the
ancient trees lean out over the water. A path leads away south into the
forest.

16302.name: A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest

north.description: To the north lies On The Riverbank In The Deep, Dark Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Junction In The Deep, Dark Forest.

16302.description:
The roar of a river grows louder to the north, and the ground underfoot
turns soft and wet. Tall ferns brush your shoulders as the path picks
its way between the grey trees. Mist drifts low among the trunks and
beads on every leaf. South the trail leads back to the fork beside the
giant tree.

16303.name: A Junction In The Deep, Dark Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

west.description: To the west lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

16303.description:
The path forks beside a grey trunk so vast that a dozen people with
linked arms could not circle it. From the north comes the rush of fast
water, while the southern trail sinks into a darker hollow. West the way
winds back among fallen trees. Roots as thick as a man's leg cross the
ground like the ribs of some buried beast.

16304.name: A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Junction In The Deep, Dark Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

16304.description:
The path drops into a damp hollow where water stands in black pools
between the roots. The grey trees here are hung with long beards of
lichen that stir in the faintest breeze. Footing is treacherous, all mud
and slick bark. The trail climbs north to the junction and continues
south through the gloom.

16305.name: A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

west.description: To the west lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

up.description: To the up lies Up In The Tree.

16305.description:
One ancient tree leans over the path here, its lowest limbs close enough
to reach, and its upper branches are strung with pale threads that glint
in the gloom. Knots and broken stubs make a rough ladder up the trunk
into the canopy. The path itself turns from north to west, skirting the
roots of the great tree. The forest around is unnaturally quiet.

16306.name: A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest

east.description: To the east lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

west.description: To the west lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

16306.description:
The path runs straight for a short stretch between two lines of grey
trunks, almost as if they were planted long ago. The ground is carpeted
with brown needles and the crumbled bark of the old trees. Thin beams of
weak light fall through rare gaps in the canopy. East and west the trail
continues through the deep, dark forest.

16307.name: A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Junction In The Deep, Dark Forest.

east.description: To the east lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

16307.description:
The path bends here around a mound of earth heaped over an old, fallen
giant whose roots still claw at the air. Toadstools ring the mound in a
near-perfect circle. North the trail leads to a junction, and east it
runs on beneath the grey trees. Somewhere far off the river murmurs,
more felt than heard.

16308.name: A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest

east.description: To the east lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Junction In The Deep, Dark Forest.

16308.description:
The path squeezes between two huge grey trunks so close together that
their roots have knotted into one. Thick moss hangs from the low
branches like ragged curtains. The trail turns here, leading east along
the forest floor and south back to the junction. Little light reaches
the ground, and the earth is damp and black underfoot.

16309.name: A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest

east.description: To the east lies A Junction In The Deep, Dark Forest.

west.description: To the west lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

16309.description:
Fallen trees lie across the path in several places, and the trail climbs
over and around their rotting bulk. Fungus in pale shelves grows from
the dead wood, glistening faintly in the gloom. The great grey trees
stand silent all around, their crowns lost in shadow. The path leads
east to another junction and west among the knotted trunks.

16310.name: A Junction In The Deep, Dark Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Small Path Through The Deep, Dark Forest.

west.description: To the west lies A Junction In Light Forest.

16310.description:
Ancient grey trees close in overhead, and the light dims to a green
twilight at this fork in the path. One trail winds north between massive
trunks, and another bends south through a tangle of roots. West the
trees thin and brighten into lighter forest. The air is cool and still,
heavy with the smell of moss and rotting wood.

16311.name: A Junction In Light Forest

east.description: To the east lies A Junction In The Deep, Dark Forest.

south.description: To the south lies The Fortress Outpost.

west.description: To the west lies A Small Path Through The Light Forest.

16311.description:
Three paths meet beneath a broad beech here, its bark scarred with old
carved marks. South a narrow track leads toward a fortress outpost
hidden in the trees, while west the path continues through the light
forest. East the trees grow suddenly taller and greyer, marking the edge
of the Deep, Dark Forest. A tumbled cairn of stones stands at the
meeting of the ways.

extra_descs.cairn stones:
The cairn is knee-high and carelessly kept, its top stones scattered in
the leaves. One flat stone at its base bears a scratched arrow pointing
toward the outpost track.

16312.name: A Small Path Through The Light Forest

east.description: To the east lies A Junction In Light Forest.

west.description: To the west lies A Small Path Through The Light Forest.

16312.description:
The path dips through a hollow where a little brook crosses it over
smooth pebbles, easy to step across. Hazel and rowan grow close along
the banks, bright with berries in their season. The canopy is open here,
and the sky shows plain between the leaves. The trail climbs out east
toward a junction and west toward the fringe of the trees.

16313.name: The Fortress Outpost

north.description: To the north lies A Junction In Light Forest.

16313.description:
A rough lookout post squats among the pale trunks of the Light Forest, a
platform of lashed poles raised a man's height above the ferns. Its
ladder has rotted through at the third rung, and the brushwood screen
that once hid it has gone brown and brittle. A cold firepit ringed with
river stones sits beneath it, half buried in leaf litter. The only path
is a narrow deer track leading north to a junction among the trees.

16314.name: A Small Path Through The Light Forest

east.description: To the east lies A Small Path Through The Light Forest.

west.description: To the west lies At The Fringe Of The Forest.

16314.description:
A narrow path threads between slender trees whose leaves let the
sunlight through in shifting patches. Ferns crowd the edges of the
trail, and the ground is soft with last year's leaves. Here and there a
branch has been cut cleanly away to keep the way open. The path runs
east deeper into the woods and west toward the edge of the forest.

16315.name: At The Fringe Of The Forest

east.description: To the east lies A Small Path Through The Light Forest.

west.description: To the west lies Outside The Barricade Gate.

16315.description:
The forest thins abruptly here, as if it had been cut back with axes,
and stumps stand in ragged rows among the bracken. West the trees give
way to a clearing before a timber barricade, its sharpened tops plain
against the mountain behind. East a small path leads back into the light
forest of birch and young oak. The smell of old cookfires hangs faintly
on the wind.

16316.name: Outside The Barricade Gate

north.description: To the north lies The Northern End Of The Barricade.

east.description: To the east lies At The Fringe Of The Forest.

south.description: To the south lies The Southern End Of The Barricade.

16316.description:
A wall of sharpened logs blocks the way here, the barricade of the
outcasts, with a heavy gate of lashed timbers set shut in its middle.
The ground before it has been cleared of trees, leaving a bare stretch
of stumps and trampled bracken where nothing could approach unseen. The
barricade runs north and south toward its two ends, and east the fringe
of the forest closes in again. The stakes are blackened in places where
fire was once set against them.

16317.name: The Southern End Of The Barricade

north.description: To the north lies Outside The Barricade Gate.

16317.description:
The timber barricade comes to an end here against a jumble of boulders
fallen from the mountain wall. Sharpened stakes, grey with age and
lichen, lean outward over a ditch choked with nettles and dead leaves.
Someone has wedged fresh logs into a gap near the bottom, the bark still
on them. The trampled grass along the ditch leads back north to the
barricade gate.

16318.name: The Northern End Of The Barricade

south.description: To the south lies Outside The Barricade Gate.

16318.description:
Here the stakes of the barricade meet the bare rock of the mountain and
leave no way around. Brambles have grown thick along the foot of the
wall, half hiding old pits dug to catch the unwary. The only way on is
back south along the barricade to the gate. Above, the mountain wall
climbs grey and sheer into drifting cloud.

16319.name: Inside The Barricade Gate

north.description: To the north lies The Northern End Of The Barricade.

east.description: To the east lies Outside The Barricade Gate.

south.description: To the south lies The Southern End Of The Barricade.

west.description: To the west lies The Big Courtyard.

16319.description:
The barricade gate stands in the east, two great leaves of lashed logs
hung on iron straps and barred from this side with a heavy beam. The
wall of sharpened stakes stretches north and south from the gate to its
two ends. West lies the big courtyard, its ground churned to mud by many
feet. Arrow slits have been hacked between the stakes on either side of
the gate.

extra_descs.gate beam bar:
The bar is a whole trimmed log dropped into iron brackets, scarred along
its length by blows from the far side. It would take two strong backs to
lift it clear.

16320.name: The Big Courtyard

north.description: To the north lies Along The Mountain Wall.

east.description: To the east lies Inside The Barricade Gate.

south.description: To the south lies Outside The Big Cave In The Mountain.

west.description: To the west lies The Big Courtyard.

16320.description:
A broad courtyard of beaten earth opens behind the barricade, rutted by
cart wheels and pocked with puddles from the last rain. Grey cloud hangs
low over it, snagged on the peaks of the mountain. The barricade gate
stands close by to the east, and the dark mouth of the big cave yawns in
the rock to the south. A broken water trough lies on its side near a
hitching rail with no horses left to tie. The courtyard stretches on
west, and to the north a path follows the foot of the mountain wall.

16321.name: The Big Courtyard

north.description: To the north lies Along The Mountain Wall.

east.description: To the east lies The Big Courtyard.

south.description: To the south lies Along The Mountain Wall.

west.description: To the west lies Along The Mountain Wall.

16321.description:
Here the courtyard runs close under the mountain, whose grey cliffs
crowd in on three sides and throw the ground into shadow for half the
day. In the middle stands a weathered whipping post, its iron ring
rusted fast. Over the turf roofs of the lean-tos the squat stone keep
and its round tower stand against the rock, a catwalk girdling the top
of the tower. Paths along the mountain wall lead north, south and west,
and the open courtyard continues east.

extra_descs.whipping post:
The post is a stripped pine trunk sunk deep in the earth, its wood
rubbed pale at the height of a man's wrists. The iron ring at its top
has rusted solid, and the ground around its foot is trodden bare.

16322.name: Along The Mountain Wall

north.description: To the north lies Where The Mountain Bends.

east.description: To the east lies The Big Courtyard.

south.description: To the south lies Where The Mountain Bends.

16322.description:
Ramshackle sheds lean against the foot of the mountain wall here, built
of salvaged planks and roofed with bark and turf. Most stand empty,
their doors hanging from leather hinges and their floors given over to
dead leaves. A gutter scraped into the ground carries runoff from the
cliff along the row. The courtyard opens to the east, and the path
follows the rock north and south to the places where the mountain bends.

16323.name: Where The Mountain Bends

north.description: To the north lies Along The Mountain Wall.

east.description: To the east lies Along The Mountain Wall.

16323.description:
The mountain wall turns sharply here, its cliff folding round a corner
of the courtyard like the crook of an elbow. Rockfall has piled up in
the angle, a slope of broken stone and boulders furred with green moss.
An iron spike is driven deep into the cliff at head height, a frayed and
rotten rope still knotted to it. Paths along the foot of the rock lead
north and east, following the wall both ways.

16324.name: Along The Mountain Wall

north.description: To the north lies The Big Courtyard.

east.description: To the east lies Outside The Big Cave In The Mountain.

south.description: To the south lies A Manmade Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies Where The Mountain Bends.

16324.description:
A strip of stony ground runs at the foot of the mountain wall, strewn
with scree that has rattled down from the heights. Set into the cliff to
the south is a squared doorway of heavy planks, the rock around it
chiselled smooth by human hands. Thin grass and thistles grow along the
base of the rock, and water seeps in dark streaks down its face. The
wall leads east to the big cave and west to where the mountain bends,
while the courtyard opens north.

16325.name: Outside The Big Cave In The Mountain

north.description: To the north lies The Big Courtyard.

east.description: To the east lies The Southern End Of The Barricade.

south.description: To the south lies Inside The Blacksmith's Cave.

west.description: To the west lies Along The Mountain Wall.

16325.description:
The mountain's rock leans out overhead in a great sooty lip, roofing a
wide hollow at the mouth of the big cave. The air is warm and smells of
coal smoke and hot iron, drifting from a heavy door of iron-banded
planks set into the rock to the south. Cinders crunch underfoot, trodden
into the stone floor by many boots. Grey light from the courtyard spills
in from the north, while the rock face runs on west along the mountain
wall and the end of the barricade lies east.

16326.name: The Southern End Of The Barricade

north.description: To the north lies Inside The Barricade Gate.

west.description: To the west lies Outside The Big Cave In The Mountain.

16326.description:
From the inner side the barricade is a crude thing, its logs braced with
slanting props and bound with rusted chain where the rope has rotted. A
firing step of split planks runs along it, sagging in the middle where a
support has given way. The stockade ends here against the rock of the
mountain, and the packed earth turns west toward the black mouth of a
great cave. The gate stands a short walk north along the wall of stakes.

16327.name: The Northern End Of The Barricade

south.description: To the south lies Inside The Barricade Gate.

west.description: To the west lies Along The Mountain Wall.

16327.description:
The timber barricade ends here against the foot of the mountain, its
sharpened stakes lashed together and packed at the base with earth and
rubble. A rickety platform of planks gives a view over the top toward
the forest beyond. The wall of stakes runs south toward the gate. West,
a trodden path follows the mountain wall along the edge of the
courtyard.

16328.name: Along The Mountain Wall

east.description: To the east lies The Northern End Of The Barricade.

south.description: To the south lies The Big Courtyard.

west.description: To the west lies Along The Mountain Wall.

16328.description:
Water trickles down the mountain wall here in thin silver threads,
staining the rock dark and feeding a muddy ditch at its foot. Someone
laid planks across the worst of the mud, though most of them have sunk
or split. The end of the barricade stands close by to the east, and the
trodden ground runs back west along the cliff. South lies the open
courtyard, bare and scoured by the wind.

16329.name: Along The Mountain Wall

north.description: To the north lies A Manmade Tunnel.

east.description: To the east lies Along The Mountain Wall.

south.description: To the south lies The Big Courtyard.

west.description: To the west lies Where The Mountain Bends.

16329.description:
The grey face of the mountain rises sheer above you, and set into its
foot is a heavy door leading north into the tunnels. A strip of trampled
ground runs along the base of the cliff, east toward the barricade and
west to where the mountain bends away. South, the land opens into the
big courtyard of the fortress. Stones fallen from the heights lie half-
sunk in the mud along the rock.

16330.name: Where The Mountain Bends

east.description: To the east lies Along The Mountain Wall.

south.description: To the south lies Along The Mountain Wall.

16330.description:
Here the cliff swings round in a broad curve, and the mountain wall
closes off a far corner of the fortress grounds. A spring trickles from
a crack in the rock into a basin someone has chipped from the stone,
overflowing into a muddy channel. Ferns and pale mushrooms crowd the
damp ground below it, and the air is cool with spray. The path runs east
along the mountain's foot and south along the other face of the wall.

16331.name: A Manmade Tunnel

south.description: To the south lies Along The Mountain Wall.

west.description: To the west lies At The Bottom Of A Stone Staircase.

16331.description:
This short tunnel ends at a stout door in its south wall, beyond which
lie the open grounds along the face of the mountain. Grey light seeps
under the door in a thin pale line, the first in a long while. The walls
are rough here, finished in haste, and old wooden pegs for cloaks are
driven into the rock beside the door. West, the tunnel leads back to the
foot of the stairs.

16332.name: At The Bottom Of A Stone Staircase

east.description: To the east lies A Manmade Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies A Manmade Tunnel.

up.description: To the up lies A Stone Corridor.

16332.description:
A second stone staircase climbs up from this corner of the tunnels
toward a corridor in the keep above. Its steps are narrower than those
below and edged with iron strips to save them from wear. Man-made
tunnels lead away east and south. A cold draught pours down the
stairwell, carrying the smell of the open air.

16333.name: A Manmade Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies At The Bottom Of A Stone Staircase.

south.description: To the south lies Outside The Grieving Griffon.

west.description: To the west lies Inside The Church Of Outcasts.

16333.description:
A door in the west wall leads into the Church Of Outcasts, its lintel
carved with a simple circle broken by a single gap. The walls nearby
have been whitewashed, though the damp has bled grey streaks through the
lime. To the south lies the little tavern square, and north the tunnel
reaches the foot of another stone staircase. The quiet here feels
deliberate, as if the rock itself were holding its breath.

extra_descs.lintel circle carving:
The circle is cut deep and clean, but a finger's width of it has been
left uncarved, so that it never quite closes. It is the only ornament on
the whole doorway.

16334.name: Outside The Grieving Griffon

north.description: To the north lies A Manmade Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies A Manmade Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies The Grieving Griffon.

16334.description:
The tunnel widens into a small square here before the door of the
Grieving Griffon, the outcasts' tavern, which opens in the west wall.
Above the door hangs a carved wooden sign of a griffon with its head
bowed and its wings drooping. The smell of stale ale and old pipe smoke
hangs thick in the air. Man-made tunnels run off north and south through
the rock.

extra_descs.sign griffon carved:
The griffon is carved from a single slab of dark wood, its beak tucked
against its breast as if in mourning. Someone has painted a single white
tear beneath its eye, now flaking away.

16335.name: A Manmade Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Outside The Grieving Griffon.

south.description: To the south lies At The Top Of A Stone Staircase.

west.description: To the west lies Inside The Hospital.

16335.description:
This tunnel was cut with care, its walls squared and its ceiling arched
in neat courses of chisel marks. A door on the west side bears a crude
red cross painted on its planks, marking the hospital beyond. North the
tunnel leads toward the smell of an alehouse, and south it ends at the
head of a stone stair. Torches once burned in the brackets here, and
only black stains remain above them.

16336.name: At The Top Of A Stone Staircase

north.description: To the north lies A Manmade Tunnel.

east.description: To the east lies A Manmade Tunnel.

down.description: To the down lies At The Bottom Of A Stone Staircase.

16336.description:
The stairs end on a landing hewn square out of the rock, with iron torch
brackets fixed in its walls. Smooth, man-made tunnels lead off north and
east, their floors levelled and swept. A worn stair drops down into the
rougher dark below. The air here is drier, and a smell of smoke and
cooking drifts faintly from the north.

16337.name: A Manmade Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Along The Mountain Wall.

west.description: To the west lies At The Top Of A Stone Staircase.

16337.description:
A tunnel has been hacked straight into the mountain here, its rock walls
bearing the even scars of picks and chisels. The air is cold and damp,
and drops of water fall from the low ceiling to spatter in shallow
puddles on the floor. A door of heavy planks closes off the way north to
the open air along the mountain wall. The passage runs west into
darkness, where a stone staircase begins.

16338.name: Inside The Church Of Outcasts

east.description: To the east lies A Manmade Tunnel.

16338.description:
The church of the outcasts is a long chamber cut into the mountain, its
walls left rough but its floor laid with smooth flagstones. Rows of
crude benches made from split logs face an altar of a single great block
of stone, stained dark at its centre. Above the altar a broken sword and
a snapped chain hang crossed on the wall, the only creed the exiles
kept. The way out is a passage east into the manmade tunnel.

extra_descs.sword chain altar:
The sword is snapped a hand's width above the hilt, and the chain beside
it ends in a shackle that has been split open. Together they say plainly
what the outcasts worshipped here: the breaking of whatever once held
them.

16339.name: The Grieving Griffon

east.description: To the east lies Outside The Grieving Griffon.

west.description: To the west lies A Storage Room.

16339.description:
The Grieving Griffon is a tavern carved out of the rock, warm and low-
ceilinged, with a bar of planks laid across upturned barrels. Above the
bar hangs a painted sign of a griffon weeping into a tankard, its paint
flaking away. Tables and stools are scattered about, many wobbling on
uneven legs, and the floor is sticky with old ale. A door east leads out
to the tunnel, and another in the west wall opens into a storage room.

extra_descs.sign griffon:
The griffon on the sign is painted with more feeling than skill, a great
tear rolling down its beak into a foaming tankard. Beneath it someone
has carved the words: drink, for we cannot go home.

16340.name: A Storage Room

east.description: To the east lies The Grieving Griffon.

16340.description:
Casks and kegs fill this back room of the tavern, stacked against the
rough rock in racks of split timber. Most have been tapped dry, and the
sour reek of spilled ale and vinegar soaks the air. Cobwebs drape the
highest racks, and the floor is stained dark around a split keg that
leaked out its last long ago. The door east leads back into the Grieving
Griffon.

16341.name: Inside The Hospital

east.description: To the east lies A Manmade Tunnel.

16341.description:
The hospital is a quiet chamber hollowed into the mountain, lined with
narrow cots under coarse grey blankets. A stone table in the middle
bears dark old stains and a row of iron rings for straps, and shelves
above it hold bundles of dried herbs gone to dust. The smell of vinegar
and bitter herbs still lingers in the cool air. A passage leads east to
the manmade tunnel.

16342.name: Inside The Blacksmith's Cave

north.description: To the north lies Outside The Big Cave In The Mountain.

16342.description:
The cave opens into a smoky chamber of raw rock, its roof blackened by
years of forge fire. A great stone forge built against the back of the
cave still holds a bed of grey ash, and a battered anvil squats on a
tree stump beside it. Empty iron hooks are driven into the rock where
tongs and hammers once hung, and a quenching trough cut into the floor
holds a skin of scummy water. The only way out is the heavy door to the
north, back to the mouth of the big cave.

16343.name: At The Bottom Of The Spiral Staircase

south.description: To the south lies A Stone Corridor.

up.description: To the up lies On Top Of The Spiral Staircase.

16343.description:
The base of the tower is a cramped round chamber, its curved walls of
heavy blocks rising into shadow. A spiral staircase of worn stone treads
coils up around a central column, each step dished in the middle by
countless feet. A rope rail threaded through iron rings follows the
stair upward. A low doorway leads south back into the stone corridor.

16344.name: A Stone Corridor

north.description: To the north lies At The Bottom Of The Spiral Staircase.

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies A Huge Dining Hall.

west.description: To the west lies A Stone Corridor.

16344.description:
This is a crossing of passages at the heart of the keep, where four ways
meet beneath a low vaulted ceiling. To the north the foot of a spiral
staircase winds up into the tower, and to the south a wide doorway opens
into a great dining hall that still smells of grease and woodsmoke. An
iron chandelier hangs from a chain overhead, its candle cups empty. The
corridor runs on east and west.

16345.name: A Stone Corridor

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies A Large Room With Beds.

west.description: To the west lies A Stone Corridor.

16345.description:
A doorway in the south wall of this corridor opens into a large room
full of beds, from which comes a stale smell of sweat and mildew. The
flagstones here are smeared with tracked-in mud, long dried to a pale
crust. A heavy beam spans the ceiling, carved with initials and dates by
bored hands. The corridor goes on east and west from the doorway.

16346.name: A Stone Corridor

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

west.description: To the west lies A Stone Corridor.

16346.description:
The corridor bends here, and the corner is darker than the rest, the
nearest arrow slit having been blocked up with rubble and mortar. A cold
draught creeps along the floor from the north, where a stair leads down
out of the keep. Cobwebs hang thick in the angle of the ceiling, grey
with dust. The passage runs north and west.

16347.name: A Stone Corridor

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies A Stone Corridor.

down.description: To the down lies At The Bottom Of A Stone Staircase.

16347.description:
A corridor of fitted grey stone runs through the keep here, its
flagstones worn into a shallow trough by passing feet. In the floor a
stairwell opens, and narrow stone steps lead down into the dark toward
the bottom of a staircase. A cold draught rises from below, smelling of
wet rock. The corridor continues north and south, lit only by a soot-
stained arrow slit high in the wall.

16348.name: A Stone Corridor

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies A Stone Corridor.

west.description: To the west lies Yarick's Quarters.

16348.description:
The corridor here is broader, and a strip of threadbare red carpet has
been laid along the flagstones, its edges frayed into strings. In the
west wall stands a stout oak door carved with a crude hawk, the only
ornament for some distance. Iron sconces flank it, black with old soot
and long since cold. The passage leads on north and south between the
bare stone walls.

16349.name: A Stone Corridor

south.description: To the south lies A Stone Corridor.

west.description: To the west lies A Stone Corridor.

16349.description:
The corridor turns a corner here, bending round a thick pillar of
masonry. Water has found a way through the mortar overhead, and a slick
of green slime runs down the pillar into a puddle on the floor. Someone
has scratched a tally of days into the stone at shoulder height, row
after row of patient marks. The way runs south and west.

extra_descs.tally marks scratches:
Hundreds of short scratches run in neat bundles of five across the
stone. The last row stops halfway, as though whoever kept count stopped
caring or stopped being here.

16350.name: A Stone Corridor

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

west.description: To the west lies A Stone Corridor.

16350.description:
A long, straight stretch of corridor runs between bare walls of rough-
dressed stone. Narrow arrow slits pierce one side, letting in thin
blades of grey light and the smell of pine from the forest beyond. Dust
lies thick along the edges of the floor, though a path through the
middle has been kept clear by the tread of boots. The corridor leads
east and west.

16351.name: A Stone Corridor

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies The Outcasts' Treasury.

west.description: To the west lies A Stone Corridor.

16351.description:
A low iron-bound door is set deep in the south wall here, fitted with
three heavy hasps and a keyhole the size of a thumb. The stone around
its frame is scored with gouges, as if someone once tried to lever it
open with a bar and gave up. The corridor carries on east and west, and
the air hangs colder here than elsewhere in the keep.

16352.name: A Stone Corridor

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

west.description: To the west lies A Stone Corridor.

16352.description:
Here the corridor narrows between two buttresses that jut from the
walls, so that two people could barely pass abreast. Grooves for a
portcullis run up both sides of the gap, though the gate itself is long
gone and only a dark slot gapes in the ceiling where it once hung. Chips
of fallen mortar crunch underfoot. The passage leads east and west.

16353.name: A Stone Corridor

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies A Stone Corridor.

16353.description:
At this corner of the corridor a small niche in the wall holds a crude
shrine, a stack of flat stones topped by a carved wooden figure with its
face worn smooth by touching hands. Wax drippings have pooled and
hardened at its foot in a pale crust. The air here smells faintly of
tallow and damp. The passage continues east and south.

extra_descs.shrine figure:
The wooden figure is no god anyone in Garathorm would know: a hooded
traveller with a staff, carved by an unskilled hand. Its face has been
rubbed away entirely by fingers seeking luck.

16354.name: A Stone Corridor

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies A Stone Corridor.

16354.description:
The corridor runs straight between walls hung with tattered banners,
their colours faded to a muddy brown and their devices too frayed to
read. A long crack runs across the ceiling, and someone has propped it
with a timber beam wedged against the floor. Water drips steadily from
the crack into a hollow worn in the flagstones. The way leads north and
south.

16355.name: A Stone Corridor

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies A Stone Corridor.

west.description: To the west lies The Guard Chamber.

16355.description:
A heavy door reinforced with iron straps stands in the west wall here, a
narrow spy-hole cut through it at eye level. Benches of rough planks
line the opposite side of the corridor, where sentries must once have
sat out the long watches. The stone above the benches is scrawled with
charcoal drawings of crude figures and the scores of old dice games. The
corridor runs on north and south.

16356.name: A Stone Corridor

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

16356.description:
The corridor bends here, the corner rounded off where years of shoulders
have brushed the stone smooth. A drainage grate is set into the floor,
and from somewhere far below comes the gurgle of running water. The air
is close and smells of mould and old smoke. The passage leads north and
east into the gloom.

16357.name: A Stone Corridor

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies In A Hall Of Beds.

west.description: To the west lies A Stone Corridor.

16357.description:
The corridor widens slightly where an open archway leads south into a
long hall of beds. A sour smell of unwashed blankets and old straw
drifts out from it. Wooden pegs line the wall beside the arch, where
cloaks were once hung by men coming off watch. The passage continues
east toward the heart of the keep and west round a corner.

16358.name: The Grand Armory

south.description: To the south lies The Guard Chamber.

16358.description:
The grand armory is a long vaulted room lined with racks, stands and
pegs enough to arm a war band, though nearly all of them stand empty
now. A grinding wheel on a wooden frame sits in one corner, its stone
worn into a deep groove. Straw training dummies slump on their poles at
the far end, slashed open and spilling their stuffing. The door south
leads back to the guard chamber.

16359.name: The Guard Chamber

north.description: To the north lies The Grand Armory.

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

16359.description:
The guard chamber is square and spartan, with a rack of empty weapon
pegs along one wall and a table of scarred planks in the middle. A stout
door bound in iron leads north into the armory, a heavy bar resting in
brackets beside it. A hearth no bigger than a bread oven warms nothing
now, its ashes cold and grey. The way east leads back out to the stone
corridor.

16360.name: In A Hall Of Beds

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

16360.description:
This long, low hall was once a barracks, with sleeping pallets laid in
rows along both walls beneath a vaulted ceiling. Many have been dragged
together into heaps, as though the last sleepers here made a nest for
warmth. A rusted brazier stands in the centre, its coals long dead, and
soot has blackened the vault above it. The archway north leads back out
to the stone corridor.

16361.name: A Large Room With Beds

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

16361.description:
Rows of narrow wooden cots fill this large room, their straw mattresses
split and spilling onto the floor. A long table runs down the middle,
scarred with knife marks and ringed with the stains of countless mugs.
Wooden chests stand at the foot of some beds, their lids broken open and
their contents long since taken. The only door leads north back to the
corridor.

16362.name: A Huge Dining Hall

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

south.description: To the south lies The Kitchen.

16362.description:
The dining hall is vast for a fortress of outcasts, its high roof held
up by blackened timber beams. Three long trestle tables run its length
with benches on either side, enough to seat a small army, though most of
the benches have been overturned. A great hearth yawns cold in one wall,
the skull of a stag nailed above it. A door to the south leads into the
kitchen, and the corridor lies north.

16363.name: The Outcasts' Treasury

north.description: To the north lies A Stone Corridor.

16363.description:
The treasury is a small vault of solid stone, its ceiling barely high
enough to stand beneath. Empty strongboxes line the walls with their
lids thrown back, and splintered shelves hang askew from their pegs. A
pair of brass weighing scales is bolted to a stone bench, where the
outcasts once measured out their shares of plunder. Scratches on the
floor show where heavy chests were dragged out north through the door.

16364.name: The Storage Room

east.description: To the east lies The Kitchen.

16364.description:
Shelves of rough planks line this cramped storage room from floor to
ceiling, mostly bare now. Empty barrels stand stacked in a corner with
their staves sprung, and rat-gnawed holes riddle the lowest shelves.
Spilled grain has drifted into the corners like yellow dust. The air is
dry and smells of old flour, and the door east leads back into the
kitchen.

16365.name: The Kitchen

north.description: To the north lies A Huge Dining Hall.

west.description: To the west lies The Storage Room.

16365.description:
The kitchen is low and smoky, its walls glazed brown with years of
grease. A huge iron cauldron hangs from a chain over a fire pit in the
middle of the floor, a crust of something burnt still clinging to its
sides. Chopping blocks and a stone sink line the walls, and a smell of
rancid fat hangs over everything. Doors lead north into the dining hall
and west to a storage room.

16366.name: Yarick's Quarters

east.description: To the east lies A Stone Corridor.

16366.description:
Yarick's Quarters are the finest rooms in the keep, which is not saying
a great deal. A wide bed with carved posts stands against one wall,
heaped with moth-eaten furs, and a writing desk beneath a narrow window
is blotched with spilled ink. A bearskin rug covers the flagstones, and
a tapestry of a hunting scene hangs crooked above the hearth. The door
east leads back into the stone corridor.

extra_descs.tapestry hunting scene:
The tapestry shows riders in fine colours chasing a white stag through a
forest, the work of some lord's household far from here. A long slash
runs through the lead rider, and nobody has bothered to mend it.

16367.name: On Top Of The Spiral Staircase

west.description: To the west lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

down.description: To the down lies At The Bottom Of The Spiral Staircase.

16367.description:
The spiral staircase ends at a small landing near the top of the tower,
where the air is fresher and a breeze whistles through gaps in the
stonework. A low door in the west wall opens onto the catwalk that rings
the tower, and the creak of its planks carries in. The worn steps wind
back down around their column into the gloom. Old rushes and stray
feathers have gathered in the corners of the landing.

16368.name: On A Catwalk Around The Tower

north.description: To the north lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

east.description: To the east lies On Top Of The Spiral Staircase.

south.description: To the south lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

16368.description:
A narrow catwalk of tarred planks clings to the outside of the tower,
sheltered by a slanting roof of wooden shingles and guarded by a waist-
high parapet of timber. Through the gaps between the parapet boards the
courtyard lies far below, a muddy square of sheds and lean-tos. The
doorway east leads back in to the head of the spiral staircase. The
walkway curves away north and south around the flank of the tower.

16369.name: On A Catwalk Around The Tower

north.description: To the north lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

east.description: To the east lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

16369.description:
The catwalk rounds a corner of the tower, where a small bell hangs from
a bracket under the eaves, green with age and missing its clapper. The
parapet here leans outward, its posts loosened in their sockets, and a
careless step could send a body over. The wind that slips under the roof
smells of pine and damp stone. The walkway leads north and east.

16370.name: On A Catwalk Around The Tower

east.description: To the east lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

west.description: To the west lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

16370.description:
On this side the catwalk passes beneath a row of iron hooks hammered
into the tower wall, where wet cloaks or fresh game might once have been
hung to dry. The parapet is studded with old arrowheads, broken off in
the wood from some long-ago attack. Far below, the roofs of the
courtyard sheds sag under moss and leaf mould. The walkway runs east and
west.

16371.name: On A Catwalk Around The Tower

north.description: To the north lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

west.description: To the west lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

16371.description:
At this corner the shingle roof has partly fallen in, and broken
shingles and a snapped rafter lie heaped across the planks. Rain has
soaked the boards dark and soft, and they give alarmingly underfoot.
Beyond the parapet the forest crowds up to the barricade, and somewhere
past it the rush of a fast river can be heard. The catwalk leads north
and west around the tower.

16372.name: On A Catwalk Around The Tower

north.description: To the north lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

south.description: To the south lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

16372.description:
The catwalk runs straight along this flank of the tower, and from here
the whole length of the timber barricade can be traced below, a jagged
line of stakes between courtyard and forest. Several planks are missing,
leaving gaps through which the drop is plain to see. Moss has crept
along the shaded parapet rail and greened the shingles above. The way
continues north and south.

16373.name: On A Catwalk Around The Tower

south.description: To the south lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

west.description: To the west lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

16373.description:
A corner of the catwalk juts out here on heavy timber brackets, giving a
lookout a view two ways at once. A rusted iron brazier is bolted to the
planks, its bowl full of rain-soaked ash and charred sticks. Over the
parapet the forest spreads away beyond the barricade, a rolling sea of
ancient grey trees. The walkway leads south and west around the tower.

16374.name: On A Catwalk Around The Tower

east.description: To the east lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

west.description: To the west lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

16374.description:
Along this side of the tower the parapet has been patched with
mismatched boards, some still bearing the flaking paint of an old cart
or door. An arrow slit cut through the tower wall itself looks inward
onto darkness. Beyond the timbers the mountain rises in a sheer grey
face, its heights lost in drifting mist. The catwalk continues east and
west.

16375.name: On A Catwalk Around The Tower

east.description: To the east lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

south.description: To the south lies On A Catwalk Around The Tower.

16375.description:
The catwalk turns a corner of the tower here, and the planks underfoot
have warped so that they rock at every step. Grey cliffs loom close
beyond the parapet, near enough that their cracks and ledges can be made
out, streaked white by nesting birds. Wind moans under the eaves of the
shingle roof. The walkway runs on east and south.

16376.name: At The Bottom Of A Stone Staircase

north.description: To the north lies A Rough Tunnel.

up.description: To the up lies At The Top Of A Stone Staircase.

16376.description:
A staircase of cut stone climbs up from here into the mountain, its
steps hollowed in the middle by years of feet. The stairs mark the end
of the wild tunnels, for the rock above looks shaped by masons rather
than hacked by desperate hands. A faint glow of torchlight leaks down
from the top. To the north a rough tunnel leads off into the dark.

16377.name: A Rough Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies A Three Way Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies At The Bottom Of A Stone Staircase.

16377.description:
The tunnel here is wider but far rougher, its walls a jumble of jutting
edges as if the rock was split by force rather than dug. Loose scree
litters the floor and slides underfoot with a dry rattle. The damp has
eased, and the air carries a hint of woodsmoke from somewhere above. The
passage leads north to a junction and south to the foot of a staircase.

16378.name: A Three Way Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies By A Stinking Hole.

east.description: To the east lies A Dead End.

south.description: To the south lies A Rough Tunnel.

16378.description:
Three passages meet here in a rough chamber hacked from the grey rock. A
foul smell drifts down from the north, thick and sour enough to water
the eyes. Eastward a short tunnel leads to a dead end, while to the
south the way runs on, rougher and wider. Someone has scratched crude
arrows into the rock beside each opening, though time and damp have worn
them almost away.

16379.name: A Dead End

east.description: To the east lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies A Three Way Tunnel.

16379.description:
At first sight this is a dead end, a short stub of tunnel closed off by
a fall of rubble. Look closer and a gap shows between the fallen stones
on the west side, wide enough to squeeze through into the passages
beyond. The iron-bound door stands in the east wall, its inner face
scored with deep gouges. The air is stale and still, and the rock sweats
a cold, oily damp.

16380.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies A Dead End.

16380.description:
The tunnel ends against a heavy door of black planks bound with iron,
set into the rock on the west side. Its hinges are scabbed with rust,
yet the bolt shows bright scratches where it has been worked not long
ago. Water has pooled at the foot of the door, and the planks have
swollen and darkened. Back east the dark tunnel winds away toward the
distant river.

16381.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16381.description:
Here the tunnel widens into a small round chamber, as if someone meant
to make a resting place and gave up halfway. A ledge of rock has been
chipped flat along one side, wide enough to sit on. The ceiling drips
constantly, and the floor is a skin of mud over hard stone. Narrow
passages lead away east and west.

16382.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16382.description:
A thin wind whistles through cracks in the rock here, cold and smelling
faintly of pine, as though the forest lies not far beyond. The draught
has dried the stone a little, and pale lichen spreads across it in
rings. Rows of scratches, tallies of days perhaps, are cut into one wall
at shoulder height. The tunnel leads on east and west.

extra_descs.scratches tallies wall:
Short upright strokes are scored into the rock in bundles of five, row
after row of them, far more than a few weeks' worth. The last bundle is
unfinished, with only two strokes made.

16383.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16383.description:
The floor drops into a long trough of standing water, cold and knee-
deep, with a slimy bottom that shifts underfoot. Ripples run ahead of
you into the dark and slap faintly against unseen rock. The ceiling is
so low here that tall folk must stoop. Beyond the water the tunnel
climbs out to the west, while east it rises toward the timbered stretch.

16384.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies Where The Dark, Damp Tunnel Bends.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16384.description:
Rough timbers prop the ceiling here, black with damp and bowed under the
weight of the rock above. One post has split and leans drunkenly, and
loose stones have trickled down around its foot. The walls glisten
wherever a light falls on them. The tunnel continues east toward the
bend and west toward a faint sound of dripping.

16385.name: Where The Dark, Damp Tunnel Bends

north.description: To the north lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16385.description:
The tunnel bends hard here, swinging from north to west around a great
knuckle of rock that juts out of the wall. The bulge is polished smooth
at shoulder height, rubbed by countless travellers steadying themselves
on the turn. Water drips from its underside into a shallow pool.
Westward the passage runs level into the deep of the mountain.

16386.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Where The Dark, Damp Tunnel Bends.

16386.description:
This stretch of tunnel is straighter than the rest, as if those who dug
it grew tired of following the whims of the rock. Puddles lie in a line
down the middle of the floor, each one reflecting nothing but darkness.
A faint draught comes from the south, carrying a cold smell of stone. To
the north the passage leads to the top of the climb.

16387.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

south.description: To the south lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

down.description: To the down lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16387.description:
The climb from below ends on a narrow ledge, and a tunnel leads off
south from the top of it. The notched footholds drop away down into the
dark, wet and treacherous. Here the rock is warmer, and the dripping
eases to a slow, patient tick. Old soot marks the ceiling where someone
once rested a torch against the stone.

16388.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

up.description: To the up lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16388.description:
A rough chimney rises from the ceiling here, its sides notched with
footholds cut by hand. Water streams down it and splashes into a basin
worn into the floor beneath, so that climbing up means climbing through
a cold shower. The tunnel itself runs back north toward the sound of the
river. Moss of a sickly yellow grows thick around the foot of the climb.

16389.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies By An Underground River.

south.description: To the south lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16389.description:
The roar of the river fades behind you as this tunnel winds through the
roots of the mountain. Water seeps everywhere, beading on the walls and
gathering in shallow pools that hide the uneven floor. The air is heavy
and close, tasting of stone and rot. The passage runs north toward the
river and south into a blacker dark.

16390.name: By An Underground River

east.description: To the east lies On An Underground River.

south.description: To the south lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16390.description:
A shelf of flat stone runs beside the river here, and the black water
sweeps past it into a cleft far too low for any raft. Iron rings
hammered into the rock show where boats were once tied off, though the
ropes have long since rotted away. East, the river runs back up toward
its spring. A dark tunnel opens south, leaving the water's noise behind.

16391.name: On An Underground River

east.description: To the east lies Where The Underground River Begins.

west.description: To the west lies By An Underground River.

16391.description:
You drift on a crude raft of lashed logs, the black water hissing past
its edges as the current carries you along. The roof hangs so low in
places that you must crouch, its stone dripping onto your shoulders.
Upstream to the east the river roars out of its spring, and downstream
to the west a ledge of rock shows faintly at the water's edge. The cold
rising off the water bites through any cloak.

16392.name: Where The Underground River Begins

north.description: To the north lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies On An Underground River.

16392.description:
Water bursts from a cleft in the rock and gathers in a deep, churning
pool, the birthplace of a black river that slides away west through a
low arch of stone. The roar of it fills the cavern and throws a fine
cold spray over everything. The ledge you stand on is slick and narrow,
worn smooth by years of rushing water. A tunnel leads back north, away
from the noise and into the dry dark.

16393.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Where The Underground River Begins.

16393.description:
The passage turns sharply here, and the drip of water becomes a steady
patter from cracks in the low ceiling. Pale mineral crusts streak the
rock in white and rust-red ribbons where the water has run for years.
The floor dips south, and from that way comes the hollow murmur of a
larger stream. Back east, the tunnel climbs toward the far-off trap
door.

16394.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16394.description:
Here the earth gives way to bare grey rock, rough and slick under the
fingers. Someone hacked this passage out long ago with crude tools, and
the gouges still score the walls in long uneven rows. A thin stream runs
along one side of the floor, ankle-deep in places and cold enough to
ache. The tunnel stretches on east and west, black in both directions.

16395.name: A Dark, Damp Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Under A Trap Door.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

16395.description:
The tunnel here is barely wide enough for one, its walls of raw earth
and broken stone weeping with water. Roots hang from the ceiling like
old rope, and drops gather on their tips and fall into the mud below.
The way climbs gently north toward the trap door and runs on west into
deeper darkness. Somewhere ahead water trickles steadily, a sound that
never stops.

16396.name: Under A Trap Door

south.description: To the south lies A Dark, Damp Tunnel.

up.description: To the up lies Inside The Cabin.

16396.description:
A square trap door is set in the planks overhead, and a ladder of split
poles climbs up to it and the cabin above. The rungs are worn pale by
hands and boots. Below, the earth has been dug away into a low chamber
shored with rough timber, its floor of packed mud sucking at each step.
The air is cold and smells of wet clay and old smoke drifting down
through the cracks. A dark, dripping tunnel leads off south into the
earth.

16397.name: A Secret Room

west.description: To the west lies By A Stinking Hole.

16397.description:
Behind the hidden door lies a small square room, its walls dressed with
fitted stone rather than left raw. A stone bench runs along one side,
and iron hooks are set in the wall above it. The air is dry and still,
untouched by the damp of the tunnels, and dust lies thick over every
surface. A single narrow door leads back west to the stinking hole.

16398.name: By A Stinking Hole

east.description: To the east lies A Secret Room.

south.description: To the south lies A Three Way Tunnel.

16398.description:
A ragged hole gapes in the floor here, and from its depths rises a
stench of rot and old filth that clings to everything. The rock around
its lip is stained black and slick. Nobody has bothered to cover it, and
perhaps nobody dared to go close enough. The east wall looks oddly
smooth and squared, unlike the rough rock elsewhere. The tunnel leads
back south to the three-way junction.
